title: Concordant pin resolver and performance-profile publish spec
creator: Maya Fernández
description:
Scope: define clear, unambiguous semantics for model version pinning in the public API/SDK and the runtime resolver, and specify how model performance profiles are published and consumed to support safe runtime fallbacks. Goal is to prevent accidental model drift, make client-side validation predictable, and enable the runtime to select safer fallback variants under load or capacity constraints while preserving repeatability for customers who pin explicitly.

This ticket covers: (1) canonical precedence order for pins supplied as tag, semver range, and VCS-style commit hash; (2) reconciliation rules when multiple pin fields are present (e.g., tag+semver); (3) deterministic runtime fallback policy (exact hash -> semver range -> tag -> latest-compatible variant) with timebound stability windows and audit logs; (4) publish semantics for performance profiles (latency/cost/SLO buckets) tied to model versions and how clients can opt into profile-based routing; (5) SDK ergonomics: pin validation, warnings, and a lightweight local resolver for offline determinism; (6) deprecation and rollback behaviors for pinned releases and how the control plane emits compatibility warnings and telemetry.

We must ensure backwards compatibility with existing pin strings accepted by older SDKs and provide a migration path for customers who used opaque aliases. This spec includes API examples, error codes, event types for telemetry, and a compatibility matrix mapping runtime version to resolver behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Public API accepts pin as one or more of: tag, semver (range or exact), commit hash. Request validation returns deterministic error when inputs conflict.
Resolver precedence confirmed: commit-hash exact match > semver exact match > semver range best-match by semver weight > stable-tag match > 'latest' family. Document contains rationales and examples.
Runtime implements a timebound stability window (configurable, default 72h) during which pinned alias resolves to a locked release; outside window runtime can advance on explicit policy.
Performance profiles published to model-catalog include: 50/95/99 latency, tokens/sec, quantized-size, and cost-per-1k-tokens. Profiles are versioned and signed by the control plane.
SDK surfaces warnings for ambiguous pins (e.g., tag that maps to multiple releases) and provides opt-in deterministic local resolve mode for reproducible dev/test behavior.

Fallback policy implemented and covered by integration tests: when exact model not available, runtime falls back per documented order and emits telemetry event 'pin_resolver.fallback' with reason codes.
Documentation and migration guide published (Confluence link in links).
End-to-end e2e test exercise: pin by tag, semver range, commit hash, simulate missing node and observe fallback path with correct telemetry events.
progress_updates: 2025-02-19: Kickoff meeting with runtime, SDK, and product; aligned on precedence and key edge cases. Action: draft spec and list of error codes. (notes: Confluence draft created)

2025-02-24: Prototype of local SDK resolver implemented by @liam-oconnor; handles semver ranges using semver-coerce, emits deterministic selection when multiple candidates. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/842

2025-02-28: Runtime team spike completed: evaluated two strategies for stability window enforcement (control-plane anchored vs runtime-local lease). Chose control-plane anchored leases to avoid split-brain during autoscale. Trade-off: introduces slight control plane dependency for immediate advances.
2025-03-03: Performance-profile proto updated to include quantized-size and cost-per-1k tokens; security requested signing of profile payloads. Action: add KMS signing proof in next PR.
reviews: 2025-02-25: PM review (Jordan Smith): requested stronger guarantees around rollback semantics and clearer customer communication on pin expiration.
2025-03-01: Design review (Ava Patel): suggested adding a 'preview' flag when publishing profiles so clients can opt-in before full rollout.
2025-03-02: Security review (Rahul Mehta): sign-off pending after KMS signing added for profile publishing; noted requirement to record signing key ID in audit logs.
2025-03-04: Engineering review (Runtime leads): approved precedence order and lease model; asked for additional telemetry for cost-impact estimation per fallback event.
notes: Decision: prefer explicit deterministic behavior over implicit 'best-effort' heuristics to reduce customer surprises.
Trade-off: control-plane anchored leases increase availability dependency for fast advances but significantly simplify cross-region consistency.
Edge-case: opaque aliases created before profile signing will be treated as unsigned until backfilled; clients will see a warning but can continue to use alias until migration window closes.
Monitoring: add dashboard card 'Pin resolver fallbacks by reason' and link to cost impact estimator; add alert if fallback rate > 0.5% for a customer over 1h.
